concept.name: Breakdown
concept.definition: A price move below an established support level, range boundary, or chart-pattern lower boundary. In classical chart analysis a breakdown is interpreted as evidence that supply has overcome demand at that level; an analytical reading, not a certainty of further declines.
concept.intuition: The floor that had been holding price up gives way, showing sellers are now willing to accept lower prices.
concept.mechanics: Identified when price closes (or trades, by convention) below the watched support; a broken support level can subsequently act as resistance on rebounds (the polarity principle), and volume expansion is treated as confirmation.
concept.failure_modes: Bear-trap breakdowns occur when price dips below support, triggers stops, and then reclaims the level; breakdowns on thin volume are especially unreliable.
concept.misconceptions: That a support break must be followed by immediate collapse; markets frequently retest the broken level from below, offering a second exit before any sustained decline.
concept.example: ChartSchool documents Lucent breaking support at 60 in late 1999 and falling so fast that exit above 44 was impossible — an illustration that breakdowns can gap through stops.
